content.title: Three-Adult Proximity Relay | Foreground Occlusion and Continuous Handoff
content.summary: Three research guides hand off through hair and hood occlusions before a group walk. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One continuous room axis survives every swap. + Each person is established by a complete wardrobe proof. + A real foreground body occlusion motivates each reveal. + Camera direction remains continuous across the occlusion. + The final group view proves all revealed people share the space.
quick_start.recommended_input: Begin at the boots of one adult polar-research guide in a glass conservatory and rise to her complete rust uniform. Use that braid occlusion to reveal a second adult guide in a teal uniform at the same mark. Widen as all three guides advance together along the original floor seam.
required_anchors: One continuous room axis survives every swap.
Each person is established by a complete wardrobe proof.
Camera direction remains continuous across the occlusion.
The final group view proves all revealed people share the space.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Three research guides hand off through hair and hood occlusions before a group walk. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.
